market_mistake: POSITION TAKEN 2026-09-02 ON THE CRYPTO-ORIGIN COHORT — it is THE FINDING, not a confound, and the driver is reframed accordingly. The binding tier is 67% crypto-origin before and after every magnitude gate, so the property is ungateable and had to be explained rather than left standing. The disclosure-incentive reading (they publish contracts to prove the pivot) does not survive the size and counterparty quality of what is disclosed: a 401 MW 20-year lease to Anthropic, 378 MW to a Google-credit-supported Fluidstack, $36.2bn to CoreWeave and investment-grade hyperscalers, are not manufacturable as disclosure theatre. The better explanation is that these parties HOLD THE BOTTLENECK ASSET: energized, grid-interconnected sites at scale, acquired for bitcoin mining and redeployable to AI. RIOT owns its Rockdale 700 MW interconnection fee simple; WULF has ~1,007 MW contracted. THE DRIVER IS THEREFORE POWERED INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT 'NEOCLOUDS'. WHAT THE CARD CLAIMS: the market prices holders of energized interconnected capacity as bitcoin miners and financing vehicles, when the scarce asset in an AI compute buildout is the POWER and the INTERCONNECTION rather than the building or the GPU — and the parties holding it already, having bought it for another purpose, can contract it fastest. BOUNDARY DECLARED 2026-09-02 — ORCL IS INSIDE the scaled-cloud set (operator's ruling). BASIS, OPERATOR-SUPPLIED and NOT verified by this repo (its own scan read of ORCL is `quantified-revenue-share`): Oracle is priced explicitly as an AI compute platform — $638bn RPO (+363% YoY), OCI +93% to $5.8bn — and its live debate is backlog CONVERSION. CONSEQUENCE TAKEN RATHER THAN SOFTENED: the CLASS claim about scaled clouds is WITHDRAWN, because the scaled cloud the market already credits as a compute winner is also the one quantifying its revenue share. Only the three names that neither quantify nor are priced primarily as compute platforms — MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL — remain, and the claim about THEM is that the market's attribution is untested. THE DISCLOSURE ASYMMETRY IS NOT THE EVIDENCE AND ITS CAUSE IS NOT STRUCTURAL. ORCL and BABA reach quantified-revenue-share at scale, so aggregation is a CHOICE — and that retraction licenses no reverse inference: choice-not-structure still does not permit reading attribution off the FORM of disclosure. Disclosure measures INCENTIVE, never economics. The big three's AI-compute economics are NOT MEASURABLE from their filings in either direction, which is why this card rests on CONVERSION and never on who publishes a contract.
null_thesis: REWRITTEN 2026-09-02, forced by the position above: the old null said the thesis fails if 'owners of land, substation and grid interconnect are repriced as LANDLORDS rather than as holders of the scarce asset'. That can no longer be the failure condition, because the card now claims those owners ARE the finding — and the machine's own read is that WULF and RIOT disclose landlord economics and do not sell compute at all. The null must therefore attack the RENT, not the role. THE NULL: the rent is ORDINARY LANDLORD RENT, not scarce-asset rent. Contracted backlog does not convert to recognized revenue at the contracted duration; escalators, terms and renewal pricing prove unremarkable; the credit support these leases carry (Google behind Fluidstack, 'expected' investment-grade behind Anthropic) is necessary because the tenants are weak rather than incidental; and new-build powered capacity arrives fast enough that holding an already-energized site is a timing advantage of a few quarters, not a durable scarcity. The incumbency is real but worth little, the market's pricing of these names as miners with a property portfolio is correct, and the economics of the layer accrue to whoever sells the compute on top.

first_confirming.trigger: At the next quarterly print of CRWV — the one name in the cohort that reports both sides — REVENUE RECOGNIZED AGAINST PRIOR-PERIOD REMAINING PERFORMANCE OBLIGATIONS rises, or the RPO-to-revenue duration SHORTENS. Accumulation is not the test: a backlog that never converts still grows, so 'contracted backlog grows' is consistent with this thesis and its null simultaneously. CONVERSION is where the two diverge. KNOWN LIMITATION, recorded 2026-09-02 rather than fixed here: after the powered-infrastructure reframing this test no longer tests the TIER. Of the six names gate v2 keeps, three are LANDLORDS (APLD, RIOT, WULF — WULF and RIOT disclose no compute sales at all) and three SELL something (BLZE storage, CRWV compute, WYFI GPU infrastructure). CRWV is a compute seller, so its conversion ratio reads the seller half and says nothing about whether powered-shell rent is scarce-asset rent. A landlord-side test — realized rent per contracted MW, escalator capture, renewal pricing — is OWED and is the thing that would actually discriminate this card's claim from its null. It is not added now because no landlord in the tier discloses rent per MW.
first_confirming.basis: one full scheduled print cycle; CRWV already discloses both RPO and recognized revenue ($60.7bn RPO at 2025-12-31 against $15.1bn a year earlier), so both sides of the ratio are published line items. Deliberately ONE NAME and ONE RATIO: an OR across five names is near-certain to trigger on something, which is a test that cannot fail. NOTED, NOT ADDED: after the 2026-09-02 boundary ruling, ORCL's own market debate is this same backlog-conversion ratio at far larger scale — which says conversion is the LAYER's discriminator rather than a CRWV idiosyncrasy, and is the strongest external support for this choice of test. ORCL is deliberately NOT added as a second trigger: two names joined by OR restores exactly the cannot-fail shape this trigger was re-cut to remove. It is an independent read to consult when CRWV prints, not part of the test.

If they converge, holding an energized interconnected site is a timing advantage of a few quarters, not a scarce asset, and the powered-infrastructure reframing is wrong at its root.
